Weighted K-Shell Degree Neighborhood

Source: R/centrality-batch69.R
centrality_wksd.Rd

The weighted k-shell degree neighborhood (Wksd; Namtirtha et al. 2018, 2020) weights each edge by the product of a mix of degree and k-shell index at its two ends, and scores a node by the sum of the weights of its edges: $$Wksd(i) = \sum_{j \in N(i)} (\alpha k_i + \mu k_s(i)) (\alpha k_j + \mu k_s(j)),$$ with \(k\) the degree and \(k_s\) the k-shell index.

Usage

centrality_wksd(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses wksd_alpha and wksd_mu (both required).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The two original papers were not read (they are not open access); the formula is the one three later papers state alike, two of them read from the page (Shetty and Bhattacharjee 2025, equations 3-4; Lu and Dong 2020, equations 2.5-2.6). They stop at the single sum above; a second neighborhood sum in the originals cannot be ruled out. wksd_alpha and wksd_mu are \(\alpha\) and \(\mu\). The source tunes them per network, and the papers that restate it use different pairs (Lu and Dong 0.9 and 0.2 on five of eight networks, 0.2 and 0.9 on one), so they have no default: without both the measure warns (class cograph_undefined_measure) and returns NA (owner decision 2026-11-26). Each must lie in \([0, 1]\), the range those papers give, or a cograph_bad_parameter error is raised. With \(\mu = 0\) the score is \(\alpha^2 k_i \sum_{j \in N(i)} k_j\). An isolated node scores 0. centrality_wksdn is Maji et al.'s additive variant of the same idea, without parameters. No paper read prints a score; the implementation reproduces the 35 values a source audit computed on two small networks at three settings. On four test networks, with wksd_alpha = 0.2 and wksd_mu = 0.9 the score ranks nodes closest to centrality_wksdn (mean Kendall correlation 0.972) and centrality_lnc (0.970), with correlations of 0.99 or more on single networks: 0.998 with wksdn and with lnc, 0.993 with centrality_gls, 0.990 with centrality_laplacian and with centrality_modified_expected_force. With wksd_alpha = 0.9 and wksd_mu = 0.2 it ranks them closest to laplacian (0.974), centrality_ked (0.968) and wksdn (0.964), with 0.999 with centrality_ksgc on a network with a single k-shell and 0.998 with laplacian, 0.996 with lnc and 0.992 with ked and wksdn on another. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Namtirtha, A., Dutta, A. and Dutta, B. (2018). Weighted kshell degree neighborhood method: an approach independent of completeness of global network structure for identifying the influential spreaders. In 2018 10th International Conference on Communication Systems and Networks (COMSNETS), 81-88. doi:10.1109/COMSNETS.2018.8328183 .

Namtirtha, A., Dutta, A. and Dutta, B. (2020). Weighted kshell degree neighborhood: a new method for identifying the influential spreaders from a variety of complex network connectivity structures. Expert Systems with Applications, 139, 112859. doi:10.1016/j.eswa.2019.112859 .

Shetty, R. D. and Bhattacharjee, S. (2025). Pertinence of contact duration as edge feature for epidemic spread analysis. Scientific Reports, 15, 10703. doi:10.1038/s41598-025-94637-3 .

Lu, P. and Dong, C. (2020). EMH: extended mixing H-index centrality for identification important users in social networks based on neighborhood diversity. arXiv:2003.03585.

See also

centrality_wksdn, centrality_coreness, centrality_degree, centrality.

Examples

centrality_wksd(regulation_net, wksd_alpha = 0.2, wksd_mu = 0.9)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>     107.64     134.40     163.00     133.44     106.72     108.56      84.48 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>     110.40     135.36     110.40 
centrality_wksd(regulation_net, wksd_alpha = 0.9, wksd_mu = 0.2)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>     149.99     208.32     276.19     202.74     145.22     154.76     109.12 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>     164.30     213.90     164.30
